key_insight: Machine-learning forecast accuracy in chaotic bluff-body flow has a fundamental ceiling set by turbulence physics, not just by model design.
engineering_relevance: This scaling law gives engineers a physics-based way to estimate when flow-prediction models will inevitably degrade, improving trust in CFD-informed ML tools.
method: Derived a predictability scaling law from a Kolmogorov-inspired turbulence framework.
Tested the theory on bluff-body flow, a canonical spatiotemporal chaos problem.
Validated the law against high-fidelity simulation results.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on high-fidelity simulations of bluff-body flow, showing an inevitable accuracy decline with longer forecast horizons.
watch_item: The result is established for bluff-body turbulence, so transfer to other geometries, regimes, or ML architectures may require re-derivation or recalibration.
paper_title: Turbulence Physics Governs a Scaling Law for the Machine-Learning Predictability Ceiling in Chaotic Flow
